title: Turn a one-line brief into a designed website
summary: Developer juliobsz published an /awwwards skill that has Claude Code turn a one-line brief into a designed, screenshot-checked site; the author says it keeps fixing until every score reaches 8/10.
agent_role: The agent writes the brief, concept, design system and code, then runs builds, audits and screenshots while a critic subagent scores the result until it meets the rubric. The human gives the one-line brief and confirms deployment.
outcome: Author claims the agent iterates until every rubric category scores 8/10. No specific site results are reported.
what_they_did: Developer juliobsz published a skill called /awwwards that builds a website from a one-line request like "make me a portfolio, my name is Julio." In Claude Code or similar agents, it writes down its assumptions, scores three design ideas and saves a style guide. It builds the site, then checks it with screenshots, automatic accessibility tests and a second AI acting as critic. The person gives the request and approves before the site goes live on Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare.
how_it_went: The author says the agent keeps fixing the site until the critic scores every category at 8/10. No results for specific sites are reported.
worth_knowing: The checking step needs an AI model that can read images, so it can look at its own screenshots. The author says real details, like your name, work, location and two or three real projects, give a better site.
prompt: Build me a website: [one-line brief, e.g. a portfolio for my architecture studio in [city]]. Here are some real details: [your name], [what you do], [two or three real projects]. Write your assumptions down instead of asking a long list of questions. Propose three concepts, pick one and explain why, then write a design system to DESIGN.md. Build the site, run a production build, and take Playwright screenshots on desktop, mobile and reduced motion. Run an axe accessibility check and fix what you find. Don't use lorem ipsum or invented metrics; mark any placeholders and list them at the end. Show me the result and wait for my approval before deploying.

curation.rationale: The README lays out a detailed multi-step agent workflow with a browser-screenshot QA loop and a critic subagent, and there is a demo video. It reports no concrete built site or measured outcome, and agent-built websites are a common use case.
